extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, agency counsel, environmental planners and program managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements on public outreach/notification, document availability, public meetings, and deadlines/schedules for NEPA environmental assessments (EAs) and environmental impact statements (EISs). Focuses on §1501.9 (outreach/notification) and §1501.10 (deadlines/schedules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies shall conduct outreach and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Revises introductory text to require agencies (“shall”) to conduct outreach and notification (combined §1501.9(c)), rather than recommend (“should”), to ensure consistency and avoid implying optional requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change clarifies obligations and aligns with 1978 and 2020 regulations; does not create new obligations but clarifies which provisions are obligatory. CEQ added “as appropriate” to qualify early engagement in paragraph (c)(2) to indicate engagement should occur early when regulations require or encourage it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite likely affected agencies and governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to invite likely affected agencies and governments (including cooperating agencies) to participate early in the NEPA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tracks prior 40 CFR provisions; CEQ added “any” to acknowledge there may be no likely affected agencies for some actions. Requirement is to invite participation as early as practicable; lead agency role remains supervisory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct early engagement with affected or interested members of the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall conduct early engagement, as appropriate, with likely affected or interested members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added “as appropriate” to emphasize early engagement where regulations require or encourage it; agencies may tailor engagement strategies considering scope, scale, complexity, degree of public interest, and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor outreach strategies to context
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must tailor engagement strategies considering scope, scale, complexity of the proposed action and alternatives, degree of public interest, and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility for agencies to select appropriate methods based on circumstances; ties into requirement to consider ability of affected parties to access electronic media and primary language when selecting methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider access to electronic media and primary language
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting methods of outreach and notification, agencies must consider the ability of affected persons and agencies to access electronic media and the primary language of affected persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ moved prior electronic-access requirement into §1501.9(c)(3) and added primary language clause. Agencies must also consider other statutory obligations (e.g., Rehabilitation Act) when selecting methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification may be published via multiple mechanisms if adequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may publish notification through websites, email notifications, Permitting Dashboard, or other mechanisms so long as the method(s) adequately inform persons and agencies who may be interested or affected, consistent with the definition of “publish.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An NOI in the Federal Register consistent with §1502.4(e) can fulfill the notification requirement, but agencies may also use additional notification methods to reach interested or affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public notification of hearings/meetings and availability of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to provide public notification of NEPA-related hearings, public meetings, other opportunities for public engagement, and the availability of environmental documents (§1501.9(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to include an “as appropriate” qualifier here because regulations have always required such notice; agencies must notify as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify those who requested notification and those with regular subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must notify both entities and persons who have requested notification on an individual action and those who have requested regular notification (e.g., geographic region or category of actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ consolidated these notification obligations into §1501.9(c)(5)(i). Notification required in the Federal Register is addressed separately when actions have national concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register notification for national concern actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action has effects of national concern, agencies must provide notification in the Federal Register in addition to other required notifications (§1501.9(c)(5)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ changed “notice” to “notification” for consistency and clarified this Federal Register notification is in addition to individualized/regular notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-concern notification mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions primarily of local concern, notification may include distribution to or through State, Tribal, or local governments and agencies, listings in local newspapers of general circulation, and other local mechanisms (§1501.9(c)(5)(iii)(A)-(I)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ's final rule retains and consolidates the list of mechanisms and recommends establishing email notification lists or similar methods for the public to request electronic notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make EISs and underlying documents available consistent with FOIA and without charge where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must make EISs and any underlying documents available consistent with FOIA and without charge to the extent practicable (§1501.9(c)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ restored language related to fees removed in 2020 to encourage transparency and access, recognizing some members of the public lack access to electronic information and should not be charged where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold or sponsor public meetings/hearings (shall) and consider format needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall hold or sponsor public meetings or hearings where required and must consider the needs of affected communities when determining the appropriate format (in-person, virtual, formal hearing, listening session) (§1501.9(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retained “shall” rather than making meetings discretionary; agencies must consider affected communities’ needs and are required to allow multiple submission methods for electronic/virtual meetings (electronic, regular mail, or other appropriate methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide draft environmental documents in advance of meetings (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ restores the 1978 recommendation that draft EISs (broadened to draft environmental documents) be made available at least 15 days in advance when they are the subject of a public meeting or hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recommendation intended to facilitate more effective public engagement; it broadens prior 1978 language to apply to draft environmental documents generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies shall engage the public in preparing and implementing agency NEPA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to involve/engage the public in preparing and implementing their agency NEPA procedures (revising the wording from “involve” to “engage”) (§1501.9(e) final numbering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized this provision as proposed; engagement replaces “involvement” to reflect consistent terminology across the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must set deadlines and schedules for NEPA reviews to be efficient and sound
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must set deadlines and schedules for NEPA reviews to achieve efficient and informed NEPA analyses consistent with section 107 of NEPA, emphasizing that analyses should be efficient, expeditious, and include “sound” analysis (§1501.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules should be appropriate to individual types of proposed actions and promote predictability and transparency for stakeholders and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency shall consult with and seek concurrence when establishing schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing and updating schedules, the lead agency shall consult with and seek the concurrence of any joint lead, cooperating, and participating agencies and consult with applicants (seek concurrence, not obtain it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added “any” to clarify not all actions have joint leads/cooperating agencies; requiring only that concurrence be sought balances need for agreement with risk of delay if concurrence were required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory deadlines for EA and EIS (1 year and 2 years) with possibility to extend
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required, where applicable, to complete an EA within one year and an EIS within two years, unless the lead agency, in consultation with any applicant as applicable, extends the deadline in writing and sets a new deadline providing only as much time as necessary to complete the EA or EIS (§1501.10(b)(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ included “as applicable” to account for actions without applicants; section 107(g) permits extension where necessary to meet engagement and analytic obligations, and agencies have experience meeting these timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting points for measuring deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must measure the one- or two-year deadlines from the soonest applicable date: (i) the date the agency determines an EA or EIS is required; (ii) the date the agency notifies an applicant that its application to establish a right-of-way is complete; or (iii) the date the agency issues an NOI (§1501.10(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These starting points reflect section 107(g)(1) of NEPA; CEQ declined to require agencies to include automatic-start criteria in NEPA procedures but agencies may do so voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: End dates for measuring deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: For EAs, the end date is the date the agency publishes an EA, makes the EA available pursuant to pre-decisional administrative review (where applicable), or issues an NOI to prepare an EIS; for EISs, the end date is the date EPA publishes notice of availability of the final EIS or the agency makes the final EIS available pursuant to pre-decisional administrative review (§1501.10(b)(4)(i)-(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both draft and final EAs are published, the final EA is used to determine the end date. References are consistent with §1506.10(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting missed deadlines to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Each lead agency must submit a report to Congress on any missed deadlines as required by section 107(h) of NEPA; an agency that properly extends a deadline in conformity with the statute/regulations has not missed a deadline and need not report (§1501.10(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to provide further specifics on report content or timing at this time and declined to provide a pause mechanism for the statutory clock beyond the extension authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency must develop schedules and set milestones for reviews and authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate predictability, the lead agency shall develop a schedule for completion of environmental impact statements and environmental assessments as well as any authorizations required to carry out the action, and set milestones for environmental reviews and authorizations (including permits) (§1501.10(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules may vary by type of action and should be based on agency experience reviewing similar actions; CEQ may issue guidance or agencies may include additional milestones as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in setting schedules (including substantial dispute & Tribal consultation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors agencies may consider when setting schedules include potential for environmental harm, public need, consequences of delay, degree to which a substantial dispute exists regarding size/location/nature/consequences of the action and its effects (restored factor), time necessary to conduct government-to-government Tribal consultation, and court-ordered deadlines, among others (§1501.10(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ restored and clarified the “substantial dispute” factor (distinct from general public controversy) and added explicit consideration of Tribal consultation time and court-ordered deadlines to encourage building sufficient time into schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum milestones required in EIS and EA schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: EIS schedules must include minimum milestones: publication of the NOI, issuance of the draft EIS, the public comment period, issuance of the final EIS, and issuance of the ROD. EA schedules must include: decision to prepare an EA; issuance of a draft EA where applicable; public comment period where applicable; issuance of the final EA and a decision whether to issue a FONSI or NOI (§1501.10(e)-(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to add more milestones at this time, noting the list is non-exhaustive and agencies may include additional milestones or CEQ may provide future guidance recommending others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a person to expedite the NEPA process
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may designate a person to expedite the NEPA process (paragraph (g)); CEQ preserved this longstanding discretion without adding further constraints on when or who may fill the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to expand the paragraph to prescribe when the role would be beneficial or set requirements on who can fill it, preserving agency flexibility.
